title: Nvidia launches new open models to run agents in the enterprise and on PCs
slides: Can Nvidia's open models run agents on your PC?
The chips giant now ships software that executes tasks locally
But the small models trade raw power for privacy
Your team could deploy agents without cloud data leaving
Test one local agent before your competitor does
thread_text:
1. Local AI agents are here

Nvidia just released open-source software that can run AI agents entirely on your own PC—no cloud required. The catch? The models are tiny compared to ChatGPT.

2. Small models, big trade-off

These compact models sacrifice raw power for privacy. You get local execution and data that never leaves your machine, but expect slower responses and simpler reasoning.

3. Your data stays put

For teams handling sensitive info, this means deploying agents without sending a single byte to external servers. Compliance and security teams can finally breathe easier.

4. No cloud, no vendor lock-in

Running agents locally also cuts dependency on cloud providers. You control updates, costs, and downtime—but you'll need to manage hardware and maintenance yourself.

5. Try it before the hype

Download Nvidia's open models and test one simple agent on your own machine this week. Does the privacy gain justify the performance hit for your workflow?
